s: We are also developing solutions using AI-assisted therapist feedback and monitoring.
We continue to build an in-house digital team with experts in technology, engineering, and AI (which we refer to as Augmented Intelligence as well as Artificial Intelligence).

Working with third parties, we currently use digital technology in a number of ways: • An online preparation platform for participants in our TRD trial to educate them and help prepare them for their psilocybin experience; • A web-based “shared knowledge” interactive therapist training platform, complementing our comprehensive face-to-face training program; • Collection of measurements in our Phase IIb clinical trial, including remote data collection using mobile devices so patients do not need to travel into study sites for all in-clinic visits; • Collection of some digital phenotyping information through the measurement of human-smartphone interactions; and • Harnessing AI and natural language processing capabilities to potentially characterize the mechanism of change and assess therapist fidelity to our treatment protocol for psychological support.
